newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska fed cattle market quiet, no bids - trade.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska fed cattle market quiet, no bids - trade.

text.p: Activity at Nebraska cattle feedlots was extremely quiet, with no bids or sales reported as of late Monday morning, market sources there said.

Owners were asking $120.00 per cwt on a dressed basis, with packers expected to bid $117.00 to $118.00 once they decide to get into the market. Asking levels on a live basis were $74.00 to $75.00 but the pricing had met no bids.

The showlist was seen as slightly larger than last week's approximately 53,000 head. But owners continue to sell cattle ahead of schedule to meet demand. Many cattle on this week's lists were orginally slated for sale in December.
